=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:91-154 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The per-PR round count resets at the head commit's committer date (`head_committed_at`, from scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh:101-118) rather than when the commit became the PR head, so rounds for the previous head are counted against the new head.
  WHY: A commit made before it is pushed keeps old rounds in the count, so the sweep can skip or escalate a new head and contradicts the documented "a new push starts its count again". Severity disagreement: sonnet NIT, gemini unstated, minimax MAJOR, luna NIT, glm MAJOR; highest used.
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:98-154 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When `cap_scoped=true` but `cap_since` is `{}` (no row has a usable `head_committed_at`), the paginated runs listing still runs although the filter discards every run.
  WHY: It wastes about 7 API calls per tick (§14) when the head-gate annotation failed, and it cannot change any decision.
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:185-201 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: In `review_sweep_round_cap_escalate`, the comment write comes before the label write and neither goes through `gh_api_retry`, so a failed label write leaves the PR unlabeled and the next tick posts a duplicate cap comment.
  WHY: A transient failure between the two writes produces duplicate `<!-- ai:review-round-cap:v1 -->` comments. Gemini and glm raised this as a hardening suggestion only (retry), so severity is as stated by minimax and luna.
- README.md:170 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The docs (README `SWEEP_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` row and agents.d/9683-review-round-cap-and-generated-chore-skip.md) say "a new push starts its count again", which overstates the committer-date behavior.
  WHY: The wording should say "a new head commit starts its count again (by committer date)".
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
(No task gaps reported.)
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh (committed_at / head_committed_at), scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh (review_sweep_round_counts) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The committer date is not the time the commit became the PR head, so rounds for the previous head are counted against the new head.
  WHY: The sweep keeps skipping the PR until those rounds leave the window. This fails safe, and the docs should say "a new head commit starts its count again (by committer date)".
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh (review_sweep_round_counts, after cap_scoped=true) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When no row carries `head_committed_at`, the paginated listing still runs and always returns `{}`.
  WHY: It costs about 7 API calls (§14) while the API is already failing. Returning `{}` early would avoid it.
- HARDENING: return `{}` early when `cap_scoped=true` and `cap_since` is empty (about 3 lines); reword the README and agents.d docs (about 2 lines). Risk score 1.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh (review_sweep_round_counts, use of head_committed_at) | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The round count resets by the head commit's committer date rather than the PR update time.
  WHY: A force-push with an older committer date does not reset the count, so the PR stays capped.
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh (review_sweep_round_counts) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The paginated listing is fetched even when the snapshot is empty or unusable.
  WHY: It wastes API budget (§14).
- HARDENING: return `{}` early when `cap_since` is empty (3-5 lines, risk 1); reword the README and agents.d docs (2 lines, risk 0); route the two `gh api` write calls in review_sweep_round_cap_escalate through `gh_api_retry` (4 lines, risk 1).

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:91-114 (and README.md:170) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The cap resets at the head commit's committer date, not at push time, so a PR whose head commit was made locally days before being pushed still has those days' rounds counted.
  WHY: The PR can be escalated on the first tick after the push, before any round on the new head has run, which contradicts the documented behavior.
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:115-154 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The paginated `internal-review.yml/runs` listing still runs when `cap_since` is `{}`.
  WHY: About 7 API calls per affected tick are wasted whenever the GraphQL annotation fails.
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:185-196 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The comment-first, label-second order means a transient failure on the label write leaves the comment posted and the label absent.
  WHY: The next tick posts the same comment again, so each transient label failure produces a duplicate comment.
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:115-154 (PERFORMANCE) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: About 7 paginated runs API calls per tick are spent on a listing whose `counts` will be empty.
  WHY: This is API-call hygiene, not a correctness regression.
- HARDENING: skip the listing and log `outcome=read_failed reason=head_date_unavailable` when `cap_scoped=true` and `cap_since` is `{}` (about 4 lines); reword the README.md:170 phrase "a new push starts its count again" (about 2 lines). Risk score 2.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:150-154 (cutoff from scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh:101-105) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The per-head cutoff uses the commit's committer date, not when that commit became the PR head.
  WHY: Rounds for the previous head dispatched after the commit date count against the new head, so the sweep can skip dispatching for the new head once they reach the cap.
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:195-201 (label-presence check at 178-180) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When the comment write succeeds but the label write fails, the function returns with the PR unlabeled.
  WHY: The next sweep tick posts the same cap comment again, so repeated label-write failures create repeated comments.
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:98-111, 128-131 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When a valid snapshot has no usable `head_committed_at` values, `cap_since` is `{}` but the helper still fetches the paginated runs listing.
  WHY: The scoped filter discards every run, so the calls do not affect dispatch decisions.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: NONE (risk score 0).
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh:112,117-118 with scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:101-105,154 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The per-PR round count resets at the head commit's committer date, not when the commit became the PR head.
  WHY: A commit created earlier and pushed later has rounds before the push counted against it. The sweep can escalate and label `ai:needs-human` before any round of the new head has run, which violates the documented "a new push starts its count again".
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:111,128-131 | severity=NIT | confidence=3

  WHY: It burns about 7 wasted API calls per tick, and the log line reports `outcome=counted ... runs=0 prs=0` as if the count succeeded.
- HARDENING: route the escalation's two `gh api` writes through `gh_api_retry` (about 3 lines, risk 1; location review_sweep_round_cap_escalate, ~lines 196-203); reword the README.md and agents.d docs to "a new head commit starts its count again (counting from its committer date)" (about 2 lines, risk 1).
